speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for seeing me. You mentioned episodes of unresponsiveness with facial grimacing; how long do these episodes typically last, and were you able to stay conscious during them?

speaker: Patient
text: 7-year-old boy. The patient has been experiencing recurrent episodes lasting 3–4 minutes each of facial grimacing and staring over the past month. During these episodes, he is nonresponsive and does not recall them afterward. He reports a muddy taste in his mouth before the onset of these episodes. His brother witnessed him waking up, staring, and making hand gestures during one episode. The patient felt lethargic and confused afterwards.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Epilepsy (likely Temporal Lobe Epilepsy or Absence/Atypical Absence Seizures)

Based on the duration of 3-4 minutes, the specific "muddy taste" (gustatory aura), the complex motor movements (hand gestures) witnessed by your brother, and the post-ictal confusion, this clinical picture strongly suggests a focal seizure disorder rather than simple absence epilepsy. To confirm the diagnosis and localize the seizure onset zone, we need to visualize the brain and assess electrical activity.
